gates.claim: the ONE-variable complex five-term identity: for real a in (0,1) and every w off both real cuts, the Rogers pentagon sum is exactly pi^2/2. 30 pairs, including |w| = 40, w straddling both cuts, and w within 1e-8 of the real axis. This is the numerical shadow of the Lean theorem pentagonSum_eq_pi_sq_div_two, which is unconditional and sorry-free

the base region is right: on the positive real square the same sum is pi^2/2, which is where the corpus's already-proved REAL five-term identity (FiveTwoAbelFiveTerm.rogersL_fiveTerm) pins the constant. Three reflections convert Abel's arguments into the pentagon's, at a cost of 3*pi^2/6

THE NEGATIVE THAT MATTERS. The one-variable restriction is NOT an artefact of the proof. With BOTH variables non-real the identity is false, and the deviation is not even a REAL multiple of pi^2 -- it carries a non-zero imaginary part, so it is a (2 pi i)*(log combination) and not a flattening integer. So no sharpening of the same argument reaches the two-variable case

the consequence for the 5_2 lane, exactly located. The theorem REACHES the mixed pair (y_3, y_1) -- the cubic's real root against a complex one, since y_3 = 0.43016 lies in (0,1) -- and DOES NOT reach (y_1, conj y_1), which is the pair Vol(5_2) = 3*D(y_1) actually needs. Same obstruction Routes 45-46 measured, now with an address

the target is unmoved. A = sum Li2(y_j) still has no proof. G1 is a theorem about pairs one of whose members is real, G3 is a negative, G4 says the pair the volume needs is on the wrong side of it. This gate exists so none of it can be read as progress toward the sum rule

verdict.proved: the complex five-term identity for the Rogers dilogarithm holds unconditionally whenever ONE variable is real in (0,1) and the other is anywhere off both real cuts. Sorry-free in Lean, standard axioms.
verdict.negative: with BOTH variables non-real it is false, and the deviation is not even a real multiple of pi^2 -- it has a non-zero imaginary part.
verdict.for_the_lane: reaches the 5_2 pair (y_3, y_1); does not reach (y_1, conj y_1), which is the pair Vol(5_2) needs.
